input.question: What position does Luis Barranzuela currently or formerly hold?

documents.text: As the sun set over the bustling streets of Berlin, Luis Barranzuela stepped out of the sleek black sedan, his tailored suit a testament to his years of experience in the cutthroat world of Peruvian politics. The chill of the German autumn air was a far cry from the humid heat of Lima, but Luis had grown accustomed to the change. After all, it had been five years since he made the bold decision to leave his mark on the European stage. As he strode towards the imposing glass and steel structure of the Bundestag, the German parliament, Luis couldn't help but feel a sense of pride. Who would have thought that a small-town boy from Arequipa would one day become a deputy in the German government? The thought still brought a hint of a smile to his lips as he flashed his ID to the security guard and made his way to the chamber. Inside, the hum of debate and negotiation filled the air, a cacophony of languages and accents that Luis had grown to love. He exchanged nods and greetings with his colleagues, his fluency in German earning him a reputation as a bridge-builder between the Latin American and European communities. As he took his seat, Luis's gaze fell upon the worn leather-bound book lying open on his desk. It was a collection of speeches by his idol, the great Peruvian leader Víctor Raúl Haya de la Torre. Luis had often found solace in the words of the APRA founder, and today was no exception. The weight of responsibility as a member of the Bundestag could be crushing at times, but Luis drew strength from the knowledge that he was part of a long line of visionaries who had dared to challenge the status quo. The session was about to begin, and Luis took a deep breath, his mind racing with the intricacies of the upcoming debate on EU-Latin American trade relations. As the president of the Bundestag called the meeting to order, Luis's eyes locked onto the podium, his thoughts already racing ahead to the impassioned speech he would deliver later that day.
